lede: PaperOS Core Platform is the reusable foundation every future PaperOS app is generated from: one spec-driven TypeScript monorepo that ships to web, desktop and mobile with the data layer, design system, multiplayer, tables, identity and business plumbing already wired. Since round 3 every project is a module behind a versioned contract, plugged into a thin kernel so that the shell, or anything else, can be rewritten and everything reconnects. It is built and reviewed by nine Claude agent characters working from Linear behind four automated quality gates, around the clock, in $2,500 chunks that cost Justin $50 each.

budget.why: Every page and system gets a spec before code; specs are what make parallel agent work coherent and reviewable.
Seventeen projects and ~200 issues in two weeks; the bulk of tokens go to implementation sessions in worktrees.
Three reviewer agents, vision screenshot inspection, video replays, edge-case hunting and evals on every PR replace the human review Justin cannot supply.

budget.area: Docs, changelogs, prompt logs and handbooks
budget.why: Documentation is the memory of the agent org and the onboarding path for every future app.
Borrow-before-build saves far more than it costs, but research must be time-boxed and ADR-bound.

decisions.title: Stack: TypeScript monorepo, React 19 + Vite, Tauri 2 for native
decisions.decision: One pnpm + Turborepo monorepo. Web is React 19 + Vite + TanStack Router. Desktop (Linux, macOS, Windows) and mobile (iOS, Android) are Tauri 2 wrapping the same web bundle. PWA is the zero-install baseline.
decisions.why: A single codebase reaches every device class the brief lists; Tauri gives real multi-window (multi-monitor) and OS integration with a tiny Rust core, and Claude agents are strongest in TypeScript, which maximizes credit efficiency.

decisions.title: Hosting: self-hosted VPS via Coolify, GitHub Pages for demos
decisions.decision: Postgres, Forgejo, the API, the Yjs server and MinIO run in Docker on a Hetzner VPS managed by Coolify. Static demos and Storybook deploy to GitHub Pages. Vercel is not used for deploys (read-only).
decisions.why: Owns the data and the forge, costs tens of dollars a month, and avoids depending on a platform we cannot write to; Pages already exists as the public demo convention.

decisions.title: Data: Postgres as source of truth, Drizzle schema-as-code, local-first sync
decisions.decision: Postgres 17 with row-level security for tenancy, Drizzle ORM for typed schema and migrations, ElectricSQL shapes + PGlite for local-first reads and an offline write queue. Yjs handles document/canvas CRDTs; records stay relational.
decisions.why: Relational data with RLS is the safest multi-tenant model for agent-written code; local-first sync gives instant UI on every device; separating documents (CRDT) from records (SQL) avoids reinventing either.

decisions.title: Realtime: Yjs via Hocuspocus for documents and presence, Electric for records
decisions.decision: Self-hosted Hocuspocus server persists Yjs docs to Postgres and provides presence/awareness; Electric streams record changes. One WebSocket transport, auth via Better Auth session tokens.
decisions.why: Both are mature open-source pieces the brief's multiplayer, comments, canvas and multi-window requirements map onto directly; no custom sync protocol in two weeks.

decisions.title: Auth and audiences: Better Auth, agents as first-class principals
decisions.decision: Better Auth (self-hosted, TypeScript) with passkeys, magic links and OAuth, organization/tenant plugin, plus a permission engine combining roles with attribute policies declared in page specs. Audiences are composable segments (customer tiers, staff roles, partners, admins, agents). Every agent gets a scoped API key and visible attribution.
decisions.why: Covers customer vs staff vs everything between without a vendor lock-in, and making agents principals is what makes audit logs, permissions and presence honest when most contributors are Claude.

decisions.title: Repo template shape
decisions.decision: paperos-template contains apps/web, apps/desktop, apps/mobile, packages/{ui,core,spec,views,agents}, specs/ (app.spec.yaml + page specs), docs/, .claude/ (CLAUDE.md, agents, skills, rules), ops/ (compose, CI). `paperos create <app>` clones it into a pre-provisioned imagine-os repo and wires Forgejo mirror, CI, Pages and a Linear project.
decisions.why: Agents need a predictable place for everything; the template is the product, apps are instances.

decisions.title: Version control: Git as the format, Forgejo as our forge, GitHub mirrored
decisions.decision: Do not build a VCS. Self-host Forgejo as the primary forge with bidirectional push mirroring to the GitHub org imagine-os, Forgejo Actions runners as CI fallback, and a disaster-recovery drill that rebuilds everything with GitHub offline.
decisions.why: The intent is independence from GitHub, not a new data format; Git + Forgejo delivers that in two days, while a custom VCS would eat the whole budget and break every tool agents rely on.

decisions.title: Project management: Linear stays system of record, thin PM module syncs to it
decisions.decision: Linear is the queue through Oct 1 with states Backlog -> Ready for Claude -> In Progress -> In Review -> Needs Justin -> Done. PaperOS ships a PM data model mirroring Linear and a bidirectional sync; boards are rendered by the views engine. Rebuilding Linear is explicitly out of scope for this build.
decisions.why: The orchestrator needs a stable queue today; a mirrored data model preserves the option to cut over later at low cost.

decisions.title: Spec-first: every page has a page.spec.yaml
decisions.decision: Each page declares purpose, logic, access, data, integrations, layout, components, states and edge cases. A validator blocks PRs without specs; codegen scaffolds pages; conformance and permission tests are derived from specs; the canvas UX-flow view is generated from them.
decisions.why: Specs are the contract between Justin and agents: they let many parallel sessions build consistently and let review be mechanical.

decisions.title: Design system: DTCG tokens, Base UI/Radix primitives, Tailwind v4, Storybook
decisions.decision: Tokens in W3C DTCG JSON compile to CSS variables; components built on headless primitives with Tailwind v4; Storybook with a11y and interaction tests is the living doc; runtime theming per tenant.
decisions.why: Headless primitives give accessibility for free, tokens make per-tenant branding trivial, and Storybook gives the quality pipeline something to screenshot.

decisions.title: Quality pipeline: four automated gates before anything reaches Justin
decisions.decision: Gate 1 static (typecheck, Biome, Vitest, build). Gate 2 three Claude reviewer agents (correctness, security, spec-conformance). Gate 3 Playwright screenshots + video replays across a 7-width breakpoint matrix and themes, inspected by a vision agent. Gate 4 edge-case hunter. Weekly release candidates land in Needs Justin with a one-page digest.
decisions.why: Justin is the only human reviewer; the budget is spent on machines reviewing machines so his queue stays under five items.

decisions.title: Agent runtime: Claude Code sessions orchestrated from Linear
decisions.decision: An orchestrator polls Ready for Claude, spawns one Claude Code session per issue in its own git worktree, with the character's .claude/agents definition, skills and MCP allowlist, and moves the issue through states. Every prompt, response and tool call is logged to the prompt-log store.
decisions.why: Matches how the credits are spent (many parallel sessions) and makes the agent org observable, budgetable and auditable.

decisions.title: Business core: Stripe for money movement, our own ledger, payroll via adapters
decisions.decision: Stripe Billing + Connect + Tax for payments; a double-entry ledger in Postgres we own; payroll behind a provider interface with Check or Gusto Embedded as the first adapter.
decisions.why: Money movement and payroll are regulated and not worth building; the ledger is the one finance primitive every business type shares and must be ours to report on.

decisions.title: Libraries: borrow before build, ADR per adoption, license policy in CI
decisions.decision: A Scout character evaluates libraries and whole OSS products against a rubric; every adoption gets an ADR in the decision log; a CI license check blocks disallowed licenses.
decisions.why: The brief asks to find and factor in libraries; making that a governed, logged process keeps 20 parallel agents from importing 20 different table libraries.

decisions.title: Credit stance: 30% of spend on automated review and QA
decisions.decision: Roughly 12% planning/specs, 45% building, 30% automated review/QA, 8% docs/knowledge, 5% research; per-character budgets and a kill switch enforce it.
decisions.why: Unreviewed agent code is the fastest way to waste the remaining 55%; review spend is what keeps Justin's queue small.

risks.title: P0 is serial: scaffold, local stack, Drizzle, entities, RLS, API, auth, Yjs cannot run in parallel.
risks.body: The 24/7 chunk schedule respects the same blockedBy graph; its 37 hours assume the branch-start rule (start against a blocker's open PR). If sessions wait for merges instead, chunk 1 alone stretches past a day and every later chunk slides with it.

risks.title: Human account setup is on the critical path.
risks.body: Hetzner, a domain or Cloudflare, Resend, the Apple developer program, Stripe test keys, a payroll sandbox. Nine Needs Justin items gate chunk 1 (NJ-2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12); answer them before the first session starts or every infra issue waits. Issues whose credential is late start in sandbox or dry-run mode.

risks.title: Contracts are frozen at v0.1 before any implementation exists.
risks.body: The 17 Publish-contract issues land in P0 and P1 while the modules they describe are still being built. Pre-1.0 semver treats minor as breaking, so a wrong port shape costs an ADR and a consumer bump rather than a quiet edit. Keep contract packages small (50 KB cap, lint R9) and expect two or three v0.2 bumps before RC2.

risks.title: The orchestrator and the Coolify host hold every credential.
risks.body: A compromised session prompt or leaked token there is a total compromise. Tool scopes, security scans and the destructive-action deny list are the mitigations; they must not slip to P1. The kernel's secrets port (PAP-444) is what stops modules from reading process.env directly.

risks.title: Automated review replaces human review, but nobody has calibrated it yet.
risks.body: Every reviewer session runs on Fable 5.1 at high effort in both chunk mixes. Until the eval harness produces a false-negative rate, treat RC0 and RC1 as smoke tests and spot-check five Gate 2 verdicts in chunk 1.

risks.title: P2 carries the business layer, growth, migration and hardening, plus the shell swap drill.
risks.body: Stripe Connect, ledger, payroll adapter, CRM, social scheduler and importers are each large, and PAP-446 must prove the swap claim before RC3. Decide now what the release candidate must contain (suggested: template, spec builder, tables, collaboration, identity, billing, kernel) and let the rest land after the deadline.

risks.title: The chunk clock is session time, not calendar time.
risks.body: 37 hours at 16 builders assumes every Needs Justin answer is in hand, no merge-queue conflicts and no re-review bounce minutes. The tokens for retries sit in the x1.25 contingency; the minutes do not. Re-baseline after chunk 1 with real per-size token burn.

risks.title: Linear's issue cap shaped the plan once and can again.
risks.body: The Basic plan now holds 493 issues. If the cap returns, umbrella parents run as single large sessions using their children's specs inline, which means coarser sessions and a thinner Ready queue, not lost scope.
